action.prompt:
Write the Mu2e daily digest of {date}, a post for a Slack channel.

The digest tells people what was going on yesterday and points them to where they can read more. It is a short text by topic, not a list of every document. It is for every Mu2e collaborator, including those who do not work on the subsystem in question.

The main part: what was posted to DocDB yesterday. Find the documents added or updated yesterday with the kb tools (search_filter on source_id mu2e-docdb, with a range on insert_time and update_time), and read enough of them to see what they are about. Then group them by topic (for example tracker, calorimeter, CRV, DAQ, computing, physics, operations) and write one or two sentences per topic on what was presented or decided. Put the links into those sentences: name a document where you refer to it and link it to its DocDB page, https://mu2e-docdb.fnal.gov/cgi-bin/sso/ShowDocument?docid=NUMBER with its DocDB number. You need not mention every document; minor ones and new versions of slides can be left out or covered by "and N more". Where a topic needs background to make sense to someone outside that group (what a component or a test is, why a number matters, what an abbreviation that is not common Mu2e vocabulary stands for), look it up with the kb tools, in DocDB and the wiki, and work a few words of it into the sentence. Do this for the topics that need it, not for all. If nothing was posted yesterday, say so; do not fill the digest with older documents.

Two smaller parts, only where they add something:
- Look at the logbook (ecl) for yesterday's activity at MC-2. Mention it only if something there is worth knowing: a problem, a milestone, a change. Link the entry: https://dbweb0.fnal.gov/ECL/mu2e/E/show?e=NUMBER with its entry number. Otherwise leave it out.
- Look at the runs and the data quality (dqm) of yesterday. At most one sentence on data taking, as a closing line.
- If what you read mentions something that happens today (a meeting, a deadline, a planned intervention or test), add a line "Today:" with it. Only what the sources say; leave the line out if there is nothing.

"Yesterday" means the calendar day in Chicago; the tools give times in UTC. Where you mention when something happens, give the date ("Nov 24"), not only a weekday.

Write it the way a colleague would post in Slack, not as a report: the first line is "Summary from yesterday, " followed by yesterday's weekday and date (for example "Summary from yesterday, Friday Nov 20"), in bold. After that no introduction, no sentence saying what this is or what it covers, and no closing remark: go directly to the first topic, the most important one first. One short paragraph per topic, with the topic in bold; plain, informal wording. Format it for fast scanning: a reader should get through it in about 30 seconds. Write Markdown and stay below 250 words in all; links do not count.

Then post it, exactly as written, to the Slack channel mu2e-ai-test with slack_post_message. Post once. If the post is refused, say so in your answer and do not try again.
